budget_items.what_was_said: The town manager said a professional compensation/classification study, wanted by staff for years, would need outside funding, possibly sought at the fall special town meeting.
The prior SAP bylaw change created a small monetary award for a recognition program; the board discussed removing the money and using a plaque or small gift card instead.

Previously appropriated roof-repair money was designated for a different part of the TC Pacios building than now planned to remain in use; the board wants a fall special town meeting article to move those funds.
A member asked the assessed value of the 925 Main Street property being prepared for sale.
The treasurer/collector is preparing a tax title auction; one parcel's value was cited while discussing which properties boards want to retain.

budget_items.topic: Municipal building capital cost vs. free cash
budget_items.what_was_said: A member noted a project cost that would consume the town's entire free cash for a good year, illustrating why it can't be done through ordinary capital planning.

budget_items.topic: Municipal Building Design Committee project cost escalation
budget_items.what_was_said: A member recalled the committee's goal was to keep the prior building project under one figure, but it grew substantially before town meeting rejected it.

budget_items.topic: Cost of printing/mailing town meeting warrant books
budget_items.what_was_said: The town manager pulled up the cost of printing and mailing the full warrant book to look at postcard/digital alternatives.

decisions.decision: The board agreed to skip a general Q&A on goal-setting methodology and go straight into reviewing FY25 goals.
The board agreed the FY27 budget process/timeline is the select board's top-priority goal for FY26.
The board defined a new 'tri-board' as regularly scheduled joint meetings of the select board, finance committee, and school committee to prepare the FY27 budget.
Financial policy review/adoption (from the DLS community compact grant) was moved out of the budget goal and made objective one under a separate 'review select board policies' goal instead.
The onboarding/orientation objective for the town manager was tabled for further work rather than finalized that night.
Noted (per the town manager's contract) that goals must be finalized in writing by July 15, with self-evaluation due by April 15 and a November check-in.
Added an action item to bring a fall special town meeting article moving previously appropriated TC Pacios roof-repair funds to the portion of the building that will remain in use.
Agreed the 925 Main Street sale objective will be measured by completion of sale preparation and process, not strictly a completed sale within the fiscal year.
Removed TC Pacios and 925 Main Street from the 'municipal properties' goal draft; folded TC Pacios into the Municipal Building Design Committee objective and added the Brooks House there instead.
Moved the warrant-mailing/postcard bylaw idea into the FY27 budget goal's objectives rather than treating it as a separate goal.
Directed the town manager to report back (targeted for the next meeting) on how much ARPA money remains unspent this calendar year.

minutes.summary: The Lunenburg Select Board approved a farmers-market alcohol sampling permit for Pony Shack Cider, then spent nearly the entire meeting drafting FY26 select board and town manager goals. The dominant goal, given top priority, is overhauling the FY27 budget process through new joint 'tri-board' meetings with the finance and school committees, explicitly leaving open the possibility of a town/school Proposition 2½ override; the board also worked through goals on employee experience, transparency, municipal properties (TC Pacios, 925 Main Street, tax title parcels, Brooks House/Municipal Building Design Committee), and policy reviews, without finalizing the goals document that night.

what_happened.line: The Select Board made overhauling the FY27 budget process its top FY26 goal, through new joint 'tri-board' meetings with the finance and school committees, and left a town/school override on the table.
The board approved a farmers-market alcohol sampling permit for Pony Shack Cider Inc. for five dates from June through September.

The board drafted goals touching municipal properties, including TC Pacios, 925 Main Street, tax title parcels, and the Brooks House/Municipal Building Design Committee, without finalizing the goals document that night.
The board added an action item for a fall special town meeting article to redirect previously appropriated TC Pacios roof-repair funds to the part of the building that will remain in use.
The town manager was directed to report back on how much ARPA money remains unspent this calendar year, since unspent funds are lost after a deadline.

why_it_matters: Naming an override 'not off the table' inside the FY27 budget goal signals residents may eventually be asked to vote on a Proposition 2½ override tied to the school and town budgets.
The tri-board process would change how the town budget gets built, adding joint select board/finance/school committee meetings ahead of FY27.
Decisions on TC Pacios, 925 Main Street, and the Brooks House affect which town buildings are kept, sold, or redeveloped, with a possible fall town meeting article on redirecting roof-repair funds.
